Introduction

Rhode Island licenses Home Care Providers (non-medical) to deliver personal care and homemaker services. The RI Department of Health — Center for Health Facilities Regulation oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Rhode Island’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Rhode Island’s Regulations

RI DOH licenses non-medical home care providers. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the RI Secretary of State, apply for home care provider license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Rhode Island benchmarks: Private pay rates $24-$34/hour, Medicaid rates $18-$25/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

RI requires background checks and training for all direct care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting RI DOH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks across Rhode Island’s communities and healthcare systems.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days.
